messages:
Nina Park: quick sync: we're landing v7 that changes the status enum from string -> int and prepends kv keys with a version token. need an ops-safe compatibility tactic so existing SDKs don't explode. options: adapter with mapping table, DB dual-write, or read-fallback.
Omar Khan: dual-write on writes seems safest for correctness but expensive. read-fallback (try v7 key, then v6) cheaper storage-wise. what about mutation conflicts if both keys diverge?
Sahil Patel: dual-write solves divergence but doubles storage and increases write latency. read-fallback leaves a window where reads see old values until migrated. we can do dual-write only for tenants in transition, and prune v6 keys after grace. also add write-idempotency to avoid races.
Yuki Tan: enum mapping: map known ints->strings. for unknown ints (future statuses) we should surface a metric `compat.enum.unmapped` and pass the int through for v7 clients but for legacy clients return `UNKNOWN_<int>`. do not invent semantics.
Nina Park: agree. contract: adapter maps known enums, unknown -> audit + synthetic `UNKNOWN_<n>` for legacy. include mapping version in traces: `compat.map_v=2026-03-01`.
Omar Khan: caching TTLs: if we dual-write, set v7 key TTL < v6 key TTL so eventual prune safe? hmm could cause v7 reads to miss after v7 TTL expires. maybe better keep same TTL and rely on prune job.
Sahil Patel: operational play: 1) header flag `Accept-Compat: v7` so clients opt-in 2) tenant feature flag `compat_migration={cohort}` 3) adapter will be edge-sidecar compiled in Go. behavior: reads try v7 then v6; writes write both when cohort enabled.
Yuki Tan: add safety: adapter refuses to translate mutation requests that include new fields not present in v6 (return 422). avoids silent data loss. Also log a short audit line with `compat.translate=1` for any translated write.
Nina Park: testing: unit mapping table, integration test with racey dual-writes, cache-simulation tests, and a chaos experiment to simulate partial prunes. metrics: `compat.read_fallback=1`, `compat.dualwrite=1`, `compat.enum.unmapped=1`. create an alert for >0.05% unmapped in canary.
Omar Khan: migration tooling: write a background job that scans tenant keys and copies v6->v7 for missing v7 keys. run in read-only mode first to estimate cost. schedule iterative prune with safety checks.
Sahil Patel: rollback: flip tenant flag off and route to v6 handler. adapter will stop dual-writing. keep mapping table versioned so rollback doesn't mismatch.
Yuki Tan: DevEx note: add snippet for SDKs showing how to set Accept-Compat header and an example of handling `UNKNOWN_<n>` from server.
Nina Park: timeline: RFC final by EOD, PR for adapter & mapping + test harness next Tue, internal canary Thu, partner opt-ins over 2 weeks, full cutover 30d after.
deploy-bot: scheduling canary for compat-adapter at 1767811800, cohort=internal-alpha, rollback-window=45m :robot_face:
